title: Image of the tensor of extended cycles
statement: Let X be a scheme, F and G module sheaves on X, and D a resolution pairing for F and G as in [def-sc-module-cup-realization-complex-data]. Write S for global sections and T for its degreewise functor on integer cochain complexes. Let t:D.left.integerComplex ⊗ D.right.integerComplex → D.target.integerComplex realize D, and let p,q be nonnegative integers. Let a,b,c be cycles of the nonnegative global-section resolution complexes in degrees p,q,p+q, with c.val = D.pair p q top a.val b.val. Let ν:T(D.left.integerComplex) ⊗ T(D.right.integerComplex) → T(D.left.integerComplex ⊗ D.right.integerComplex) be a chain map whose component on every tensor summand is the section tensor map. Let za,zb,zc be integer cycles whose images through the cycle inclusions and global sections of the extension component isomorphisms are a.val,b.val,c.val. For any cycle z of T(D.left.integerComplex) ⊗ T(D.right.integerComplex) in degree p+q whose cycle inclusion is the (p,q) tensor summand of the inclusions of za and zb, the induced cycle map of ν followed by T(t) sends z to zc.

source.place: Section 20.31, Lemma 20.31.3 and global specialization; Tag 01DZ for resolution classes

proof.text: Compose the target cycle inclusion with the global sections of extendXIso. The composite is injective. Naturality of cyclesMap identifies the resulting element with the chain map component applied to the tensor-summand element.

Use the section formula for nu and Realizes t. The two input extension equations recover the prescribed input sections, and hc and the output extension equation identify the result. Cancel the injective composite.

proof_origin.place: normalized cycle and comparison diagram calculation
